name: 鄭名道
objective: This course is to analyze the macroeconomic policy, international economy, business cycles, government policy, exchange rate and other macroeconomic-related issues. The course will be taught with case studies and journal literature. Group discussions are needed.
schedule:
Week 1: Introduction to Economics - Scarcity, opportunity cost, and the economic way of thinking.
Week 2: Measuring Economic Performance - Gross Domestic Product (GDP), real vs. nominal GDP.
Week 3: The Cost of Living - Inflation, Consumer Price Index (CPI), and interest rates.
Week 4: Unemployment - Measuring unemployment, types of unemployment.
Week 5: Long-Run Economic Growth - Productivity, savings, and investment.
Week 6: The Monetary System - Central banks, the Federal Reserve, and money creation.
Week 7: Money Growth and Inflation - Quantity theory of money, costs of inflation.
Week 8: Midterm Exam
Week 9: Aggregate Demand and Aggregate Supply - Short-run vs. long-run fluctuations.
Week 10: Fiscal Policy - Government spending, taxes, and the multiplier.
Week 11: Monetary Policy - Tools of the central bank, interest rates.
Week 12: The Phillips Curve - The short-run tradeoff between inflation and unemployment.
Week 13: International Trade & Finance - Exchange rates, balance of payments.
Week 14: Final Review & Synthesis
scorePolicy:
Assignments/Problem Sets (20%): Weekly assignments applying models to current events.
Quizzes (15%): Short, regular quizzes on key definitions.
Midterm Exam (30%): Covering foundational concepts
Final Exam (35%): Comprehensive, with emphasis on policy analysis
materials: Instructor prepared material from journal paper or academic published papers
consultation: Arranged through mobile phone or email
